prompt: What is the difference between `List` and `ForEach`?
hint: One has an appearance and one has none.

choices.text: `ForEach` scrolls and `List` does not
choices.why: The reverse: `List` scrolls; `ForEach` is not a container.

choices.text: `List` is a styled container; `ForEach` makes a view per element
choices.why: Right, and `ForEach` works inside a `List`, a stack or a `Form`.

choices.text: They are two names for the same view
choices.why: `List(_:rowContent:)` is a shorthand for one wrapping the other, which is not the same thing.

choices.text: `ForEach` is a `for` loop that runs once per element
choices.why: It is a view; SwiftUI decides when to build each row.

prompt: Why can `List(model.plan.courses) { … }` be written with no `id:` argument?

choices.text: Because `Course` is a struct
choices.why: Being a struct says nothing about identity.

choices.text: Because the list uses each row's position
choices.why: It does not; section 04 shows why it must not.

choices.text: Because `Course` conforms to `Identifiable`
choices.why: Right: its `id` answers which row each element is.

choices.text: Because `List` compares the whole value of each course
choices.why: Then a rename would make the course a new row.

prompt: Which of these ids is the worst choice for a `ForEach` over the planner's sessions?
hint: A good id is stable, unique and owned by the data.

choices.text: `id: \.id`, the session's own id
choices.why: That is the one `Identifiable` already uses.

choices.text: `id: \.date`, the planned day
choices.why: Right: two sessions on one day share it, and moving a session changes it.

choices.text: An id the server assigned and sends back with every load
choices.why: Stable and unique, and lesson 12 uses exactly that.

choices.text: A string the app generated once when the session was created
choices.why: Made once and kept, it is a fine id.

prompt: `Identifiable` requires one property, `var id`, whose type conforms to ___.
`ForEach(titles, id: \.self)` shows a list of course titles. What breaks it?
hint: The element is its own id.

choices.text: Nothing; strings are `Hashable`, so they make perfect ids
choices.why: Hashable is required, not sufficient: two equal strings are one id.

choices.text: A title longer than the row
choices.why: Length affects layout, not identity.

choices.text: Two courses with the same title, or a rename
choices.why: Right: equal strings collide, and a renamed course becomes a different row.

choices.text: Sorting the titles alphabetically
choices.why: Moving a row whose id is unchanged is a move, which SwiftUI handles.

prompt: In `identity.swift`, after the first row was deleted, which row did the position-keyed memory show as open?

choices.text: `Mobile, lifecycle`
choices.why: That is what the id-keyed memory showed.

choices.text: `SQL, indexes`
choices.why: Right: a row the person never opened, now at position 1.

choices.text: `SQL, joins`
choices.why: It was the row deleted.

choices.text: No row: the position was removed with the first row
choices.why: Position 1 still exists; it now holds another session.

prompt: Which `ForEach` keeps each row's state with its session when a row is deleted?
hint: Identity has to follow the data.

choices.text: `ForEach(0..<plan.sessions.count)`
choices.why: The identity is the position.

choices.text: `ForEach(Array(plan.sessions.enumerated()), id: \.offset)`
choices.why: `offset` is the position again, spelled longer.

choices.text: `ForEach(plan.sessions)`
choices.why: Right: `StudySession` is `Identifiable`, so its id is the identity.

choices.text: `ForEach(plan.sessions, id: \.minutes)`
choices.why: Two sessions of 30 minutes would share one identity.

prompt: A text field in each row keeps a half-typed note in the row's `@State`. After deleting a row above, a note appears on the wrong session. Which change fixes it?
hint: Where does SwiftUI keep a row's `@State`?

choices.text: Give the `ForEach` the sessions' ids instead of positions
choices.why: Right: the state is kept by identity, so identity must follow the session.

choices.text: Move the note into a `@Binding` with a default value
choices.why: A binding still has to point somewhere, and the row identity is still wrong.

choices.text: Rebuild the list after every delete with a new `UUID` per row
choices.why: Fresh ids make every row new and lose every note.

choices.text: Animate the delete so SwiftUI can follow it
choices.why: Animation follows identity; it cannot repair it.

prompt: On the SQL course screen, `onDelete` passes `offsets` containing 1. What does 1 count?

choices.text: Position 1 of `model.plan.sessions`
choices.why: That is the plan, all courses together; the screen showed only SQL.

choices.text: Position 1 of the sessions the screen showed
choices.why: Right, which is why section 06 translates it to an id.

choices.text: The session whose id ends in 1
choices.why: Offsets are positions, not ids.

choices.text: The number of rows to delete
choices.why: It is a set of positions; its count is how many.

prompt: Why is `try? model.markDone(session.id)` acceptable inside the swipe action, when swallowing errors is not acceptable elsewhere?
hint: Where did the id come from?

choices.text: Swipe actions cannot throw, so any error is lost anyway
choices.why: The closure could handle the error and show it; the reason is elsewhere.

choices.text: `markDone` never throws
choices.why: It throws `unknownSession` for an id that does not exist.

choices.text: The id came from the row just swiped, which exists
choices.why: Right; where the error could happen, the screen should show it.

choices.text: Errors in a list are shown by SwiftUI automatically
choices.why: SwiftUI shows nothing for an error you discard.

prompt: How many tests did `swift test --filter Editing` run?
In `aScreenOffsetIsNotAPlanIndex`, which session did `plan.sessions.remove(at: 1)` remove?

choices.text: `s3`, the SQL screen's row 1
choices.why: That is what the person meant, and not what happened.

choices.text: `s2`, the mobile session
choices.why: Right: the test pins the bug, `["s1", "s3", "s4"]`.

choices.text: `s1`, because offsets start at 1
choices.why: Offsets start at 0, like array indices.

choices.text: None: the test expects an error
choices.why: `remove(at:)` does not throw; it removed a session.

prompt: After `plan.move(from: [2], to: 0, in: shown)` on the SQL sessions `s1, s3, s4`, why is `s2` still second in the whole plan?

choices.text: `move` only works on the first course in the plan
choices.why: It works on whichever sessions were shown.

choices.text: `s2` was moved twice and ended where it started
choices.why: It was not moved at all.

choices.text: SwiftUI restores the other course's order
choices.why: No SwiftUI runs in the package.

choices.text: The new order is written only into the SQL sessions' places
choices.why: Right: `slots` are the positions SQL sessions held, and `s2`'s position is not one.

prompt: Put the steps of `delete(at:in:)` in order.
hint: Positions, then ids, then the plan.
items: Each offset is turned into the id of the session shown there
The ids are collected in a `Set`
The plan removes every session whose id is in the set

prompt: A `ScrollView` holds a `VStack` of 8,000 `SessionCard`s. What happens before the first card appears?
hint: A plain stack is not lazy.

choices.text: Only the visible cards are built
choices.why: That is a `LazyVStack` or a `List`.

choices.text: All 8,000 cards are built
choices.why: Right: a standard stack loads its whole hierarchy when it displays.

choices.text: SwiftUI refuses a stack of more than 1,000 views
choices.why: There is no such limit; it is slow, not refused.

choices.text: The cards are built in the background while the first appears
choices.why: Nothing is deferred in a plain stack.

prompt: Match each container to the situation it fits.

pairs.right: A handful of rows that always fit
A long feed of custom cards
Rows with swipe actions and an edit mode

right_distractors: A grid of photos laid out by hand

prompt: According to the Apple article quoted in section 07, when should you switch a plain stack to a lazy one?
hint: Lazy trades layout correctness for performance.

choices.text: From the start, in every scrolling view
choices.why: The article says to start with the standard stack.

choices.text: When the simulator feels slow
choices.why: It says never to profile on the simulator.

choices.text: When profiling on a device shows a worthwhile improvement
choices.why: Right, with Instruments' SwiftUI template.

choices.text: Above 100 rows, the threshold the article sets
choices.why: The article sets no number; it says to measure.

prompt: `diff.swift` counted the changes by position for one session added at the top. How many?
Why does the id-based difference make the insertion cheap for SwiftUI?

choices.text: Because strings compare faster than positions
choices.why: The cost is in the rows rebuilt, not in the comparison.

choices.text: Four rows are the same rows, so only one is new
choices.why: Right: the others slide down with nothing in them redrawn.

choices.text: Because `difference(from:)` runs on a background thread
choices.why: It runs where it is called; threads are not the point.

choices.text: Because the new row is drawn last
choices.why: Order of drawing is not what makes it cheap.

prompt: A decoder gives each session `id = UUID().uuidString` as data arrives. What does every refresh of the list cost?
hint: Are the ids the same across two loads?

choices.text: Nothing extra: UUIDs are unique, which is all an id needs
choices.why: Unique, and not stable: each load invents new ones.

choices.text: Only the rows whose content changed are rebuilt
choices.why: Every id is new, so every row is new.

choices.text: Every row is removed and inserted again, losing its state
choices.why: Right; the id has to come with the data, as lesson 12's do.

choices.text: A compile error, since `UUID` is not `Hashable`
choices.why: `UUID` and its string are both `Hashable`.

prompt: Which of these are true of a `ForEach` over `Identifiable` sessions? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A renamed session keeps its row and its state
choices.why: Yes: the id did not change.

choices.text: Deleting a row moves the state below it up one row
choices.why: That is what position identity does.

choices.text: Inserting at the top is one insertion
choices.why: Yes, as `diff.swift` counted.

choices.text: `onDelete`'s offsets are ids
choices.why: They are positions in what the `ForEach` was given.
